verdict.rationale: Proa renders on the server through an Axum backend. It documents streaming in two modes: in-order HTML flushing, and Suspense boundaries that stream ready chunks out of order so slow data does not block the page. Interactivity comes from hydrated islands that ship server-rendered HTML plus a small JS module. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the streaming API (the evidence is homepage-level claims), and independent or hands-on corroboration that streaming speeds up time-to-interactive.

support.subject: As a developer, I can render my application on the server with streaming support to reach interactivity faster

citations.quote: Flush HTML in document order when sequence matters, or let Suspense boundaries stream ready chunks out of order when slow data should not block the page.
Proa emits the server-rendered HTML plus the JavaScript required for that island
Each hydrated RSJS island emits a small vanilla-JS module plus seed state, served with a shared runtime around 1.3 KB gzipped.
